
Tuned for this machine
  llama.cpp build: master, at ~/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server (CUDA). Its
  local patches: none.
  This build has none of BoltBeam's local llama.cpp patches, so their knobs
  do not apply: only stock flags are recommended below.
  Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00001-of-00002.gguf, 48 expert
  layers of 256 experts, 23.42 GiB of experts; 5.41 GiB of them in host RAM
  (--experts-in-ram 12 (given)).
  Host: 31.3 GiB RAM, 24.0 GiB available now, 21 GiB usable for the model;
  L3 32 MiB (sysfs index3: 32 MiB shared by cpus 0-15).
  Read from this machine and the build; nothing ran to get them.

  --cache-ram 8192 · default
    kept: the host experts (and a full pinned copy, when the build can pin),
    the tables' resident rows and the 8 GiB prompt cache fit the 21 GiB
    usable RAM
  -ub 512 · default
    llama-server's default: no prefill limit was computed here (no GPU
    target detected)
    to confirm: best over -ub [1024, 2048, 4096, 8192]
  -b 2048 · default
    raised to -ub when -ub is larger (the command does it); a prompt is read
    in chunks of at most -ub, so a -b above -ub adds no larger chunk
  --spec-draft-n-max (unset) · default
    unset: not measured for this checkpoint on this chip (no MTP measurement
    of it in this machine's facts): run Measure MTP
  -fa auto · default
    auto, llama-server's default; --measure times the other values this
    build takes (on, off, auto) writing a reply, and checks their answers
    to confirm: choice over -fa on, off, auto
  -ctk f16 · default
    f16, llama-server's default (24,576 bytes per token); the types this
    build takes with flash attention kernels for them, in bytes per token:
    f16 24,576, bf16 24,576, q8_0 13,056, q4_0 6,912. Another type changes
    the answers: --measure keeps one only when it writes replies faster and
    passes Speed up's next-token agreement gate against f16 at this context
    to confirm: choice over -ctk f16, bf16, q8_0, q4_0
  -t -1 · default
    -1, llama-server's default (its own count of the cores): with 5.41 GiB
    of experts and 26.82 GiB of per-layer embedding in host RAM the CPU
    works on every reply token, so --measure times 8, 16 threads (the cores
    sharing one L3, the physical cores and the logical CPUs)
    to confirm: choice over -t 8, 16

  Not in this build (no knobs from it): llama-moe-prefill, llama-pinned-
  copy-stream, llama-server-ckpt-min-head, llama-server-ckpt-tail-only.
